Subject: Post-demo: Security checklist & EU data transfer follow-ups

Hi Elena / Tomas —

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation and clear signal that security and data residency are gating factors for StarkBank. Per our demo and discovery, I wanted to capture the outstanding items and propose concrete next steps so procurement/security can kick off the right artifacts: 

Summary of asks you mentioned during the call:
- SOC 2 status and latest Type II report (scope: hosted API + Dedicated pools)
- Data residency options: EU-only deployment, region list, and whether cross-border replication can be disabled
- Data processing addendum (DPA) and sub-processor list
- Key management options (BYOK/KMS/HSM) and encryption-at-rest details
- Vendor security questionnaire (we should kick off the doc you sent)
- Export controls screening: OFAC/ITAR considerations for payment data flows

Attachments I’m sharing with this email: redwood-soc2-type2-2026-summary.pdf (summary + attestations), data-residency-matrix.xlsx (region+replication options).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will respond with technical details (KMS options, retention, logs/PII handling) and a short compliance deck (today EOD).
2) Elena / Tomas: please upload the Vendor Security Questionnaire you referenced (or we can import it into Secureframe) — I’ve cc’d Marissa to coordinate.
3) Ben: set up a 60-minute technical deep-dive for Secure/Infra teams (propose Wed 2026-12-08 or Thu 2026-12-09).
4) Legal: we’ll route a DPA draft via DocuSign for initial review (link to follow).

If anything above is missing or mis-stated, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks — goal is to get procurement/security comfortable enough to move to a pilot by mid-Jan.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security checklist & EU data transfer follow-ups

Ben — thanks for the clear recap, appreciated. A few clarifying questions before we bring this to procurement/security: 

1) Encryption & key management: can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) in the EU deployment, and which cloud KMS providers are supported (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault)? Is HSM-based BYOK available for Private deployments?

2) Logs / PII: do audit logs or trace logs contain PII? If so, what is the default retention window and is there a way to exclude user content from logs?

3) EU-only residency: we need to ensure no cross-border replication or backups that would transit outside the EU for the pilot. Is that possible for Hosted or only for Dedicated/Private?

4) Export controls / sanctions screening: we’ll need confirmation Redwood performs OFAC screening and whether Redwood’s platform is available for workloads that might be ITAR-controlled (note: we expect no ITAR content, but our legal team needs the statement).

I’ve attached our Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_StarkBank.xlsx — happy to have you import it into whatever assessment tool you use. Target timeline from our side: procurement kicks off 2026-12-10 and we’d like answers by 2027-01-10 to make the Jan pilot goal. 

Thanks —
Elena Novak
Head of Procurement, StarkBank
elena.novak@starkbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security checklist & EU data transfer follow-ups

Elena / Ben —

Thanks — I pulled together the short answers below and attached a compliance summary for your legal team. If you want we can run through any of these items in the technical deep-dive.

Quick answers (high-level):
- SOC 2: Redwood has a Type II attestation covering our Hosted API and Dedicated capacity as of Q3 2026. We are attaching a summary (redwood-soc2-type2-2026-summary.pdf) and can provide a redactable report under NDA. Public SOC3 summary: https://app.redwood.ai/compliance/2026/soc3
- KMS / BYOK: Supported. For EU-hosted offerings we support AWS KMS and GCP CMEK. For Redwood Private we support HSM-backed BYOK (customer keys managed via KMS or on-prem HSM).
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 default; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Logs & PII: Application-level logs do not include customer message bodies by default; tenant-scoped audit logs include metadata (timestamps, request IDs, IPs). Default log retention is 90 days for Hosted; retention can be shortened or extended on Dedicated/Private. We can exclude certain fields from logs for the pilot — will document specific fields if you confirm which are considered PII by your team.
- Data residency & replication: EU regions available today: eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For Hosted we offer region pinning; cross-region replication is opt-in for multi-region DR. For strict EU-only residency with no egress, Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments are recommended — we can run a no-egress configuration for the pilot. See attached data-residency-matrix.xlsx for details.
- Sub-processors & DPA: We’ll share our standard DPA draft via DocuSign; sub-processor list is in the compliance summary.
- Export controls (OFAC/ITAR): Redwood performs sanctions screening for account creation and access; we maintain an export control policy and escalate potential ITAR issues to legal. We do not position the hosted platform for ITAR-restricted technical data without a contract amendment and appropriate indemnities; we can document the process and provide the policy summary (attached).

Attachments: redwood-compliance-summary-2026.pdf, redwood-soc2-type2-2026-summary.pdf, data-residency-matrix.xlsx

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: import/email back Vendor_Security_Questionnaire into Secureframe and send instructions (owner: marissa.cole@redwood.ai) — target 2026-12-03.
- Ben: schedule technical deep-dive with infra/security (owner: ben.carter@redwood.ai) — target 2026-12-08.
- Legal: send DPA draft via DocuSign (owner: legal@redwood.ai) — target 2026-12-06.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through any of these items.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
